page: Vultr vx1-m-16c-128g-960s is a memory-oriented cloud compute instance designed for data-intensive processing and operational workloads. Powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC processor running at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz, the instance delivers 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 8 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading. The CPU architecture features 48 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and a shared 32 MB L3 cache, backed by vector and instruction set extensions including AVX-512, VNNI, BF16, and hardware cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA-NI.

The hardware configuration provides 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio suitable for memory-dense execution models. Local storage consists of a bundled 960 GB NVMe SSD, ensuring high-throughput local disk operations without requiring detached network volumes. The system does not feature a dedicated GPU, focusing resource allocation entirely on host system compute, direct NVMe disk access, and memory capacity.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-threaded throughput alongside steady multi-core capabilities. The instance scores in the top tier for stress-ng single-core tests, single-threaded gzip compression at 39.33 GB/sec, single-threaded bzip3 decompression at 17.52 GB/sec, and Geekbench text processing. Memory subsystem metrics reflect a strong rating on PassMark memory evaluations, with large-block memory read bandwidth reaching 88.87 GB/sec and write bandwidth attaining 45.5 GB/sec. Parallel workloads, such as multi-core stress-ng tests, multi-threaded bzip3, and PassMark database operations, perform in the middle tier.

Given its high RAM allocation per vCPU and fast local NVMe storage, the instance presents balanced resource efficiency for memory-heavy services. The primary tradeoff lies in moderate base clock frequency and mid-tier multi-threaded scaling compared to pure compute-optimized platforms. It is best suited for in-memory databases, Redis deployments, caching layers, batch ETL processing, and medium-scale web serving infrastructures requiring dedicated CPU resources.

The platform features 128.0 GB of RAM alongside 960 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, offering an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio tailored for data-dense environments. Benchmark data shows top-tier performance in single-core stress tests, decompression, and text processing, supplemented by strong PassMark memory throughput. Although multi-threaded computational workloads settle in the middle tier, the combination of dedicated CPU execution, large system memory, and direct NVMe storage provides reliable capability for in-memory caches, database operations, and memory-bound ETL workflows.
